sentences.show: Officially, nobody ever escaped from Alcatraz. But one man swam all the way to the Golden Gate Bridge, and they found him alive.
In 29 years, 36 men tried to escape the Rock.
Six were shot dead. Two drowned. Five vanished in the freezing bay, and were never seen again.
In June 1962, three of them disappeared on a raft made of raincoats. The guards said the bay had swallowed them.
Six months later, inmate 1403, John Paul Scott, decided to prove them wrong.
On 16 December, he slipped out of the cell house.
His life jacket? Rubber kitchen gloves, blown up like balloons, and tied to his arms.
Then he jumped into the freezing water, in the middle of winter, and started to swim.
Five kilometres. Through the currents everyone said nobody could survive.
He came ashore at Fort Point, right under the Golden Gate Bridge.
Some teenagers found him on the rocks, frozen, with hypothermia, too weak to run.
He woke up in an army hospital. Then they sent him straight back to Alcatraz.
He is the only prisoner known to have reached the shore by swimming. With worse gear than Frank Morris, in worse water.
So if John Paul Scott made it, could Morris and the Anglins have made it too?
Scott made it across the bay. Make it to the subscribe button too.
